deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Brennweiten' (focal lengths). The problem is to determine the focal length f of a thick lens or lens system from two image-forming experiments. The method is built so that the unknown positions of the principal planes drop out.

Data:
- First experiment: a = distance from a fixed marked point R on the lens mount to the object. c = object-to-image distance. The image is 1/n the size of the object.
- Second experiment, lens turned round ('bei verkehrter Lage'): b = distance from R to the object. c' = object-to-image distance. The image is 1/n' the size of the object.

Unknowns:
- f = focal length.
- 2x = separation of the two principal planes (Hauptebenen).
- p, p' = distance from the first principal plane to the object in the two experiments.
- q, q' = distance from the second principal plane to the image in the two experiments.

(1) Gaussian lens law measured from the principal planes: 1/p + 1/q = 1/f, written as pq = (p+q)f, and likewise p'q' = (p'+q')f.

(2) Magnification: image/object = q/p = 1/n, so p = nq. Likewise p' = n'q'.

(3) Substituting gives n q^2 = (n+1) q f, so p = nq = (n+1)f and q = (n+1)f/n. Likewise p' = (n'+1)f and q' = (n'+1)f/n'.

(4) Geometry. Let M be the midpoint between the principal planes, and let y be the unknown distance from R to M, with M lying on the image side of R in the first orientation. This interpretation is mine, but it is forced by the signs.
- First orientation: M is at a + y from the object, so p = a - x + y.
- Reversed orientation: M is at b - y, so p' = b - x - y.
- The object-to-image distance is the sum of the three segments: p + q + 2x = c and p' + q' + 2x = c'.
- Hence q = c - a - x - y and q' = c' - b - x + y. This is where the page ends.

Continuation on the next page (summarised for context):
- p - q' = a + b - c' and p' - q = a + b - c. Both x and y cancel.
- Using (3): a + b - c' = (n - 1/n')f = (nn'-1)f/n' and a + b - c = (n' - 1/n)f = (nn'-1)f/n.
- Consistency condition on the data: (a+b-c')n' = (a+b-c)n.
- If c = c', then n = n' and a + b - c = (n - 1/n)f.

In sum, this is a scheme for measuring the focal length of a thick system. Turning the lens round and combining the two runs eliminates both the unknown principal-plane separation and the unknown position of the principal planes relative to the reference mark.
errors: No mathematical errors. Every displayed equation follows from its premises.
The sign convention for y (the offset of the principal-plane midpoint from the reference mark, which changes sign when the lens is reversed) is never stated. It is implicit but consistent.
Magnification is taken as positive (q/p = 1/n). This is appropriate for a real image of a real object.

results.what: Lens equation referred to principal planes, pq=(p+q)f, with magnification giving p=(n+1)f, q=(n+1)f/n
results.modern_name: Gaussian thin/thick lens formula with principal (cardinal) points; Newtonian/Gaussian conjugate relations
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Dioptrische Untersuchungen (1841), for the cardinal-point formulation

results.what: Determination of the focal length of a thick system from two settings, the second with the lens reversed, eliminating principal-plane separation and offset: a+b-c=(n'-1/n)f, a+b-c'=(n-1/n')f, plus the consistency condition (a+b-c')n'=(a+b-c)n
results.modern_name: Focometry of thick lenses by a conjugate/magnification method with lens reversal (related to Bessel's displacement method and Abbe-type magnification methods)
results.usually_credited_to: Bessel (two-position displacement method); Abbe and others (later magnification-based focometers)

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss created the principal-plane theory (1840/41) and was keenly interested in its practical use, so a worked scheme for measuring f from it is expected. The neat elimination of the unknown principal-plane position by reversing the lens is a pleasant unpublished detail. It is not a major priority claim.

checkable.asserts: p=(n+1)f, q=(n+1)f/n satisfy pq=(p+q)f with p=nq (should be 0)

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,cp,x,y=symbols('a b c cp x y'); p=a-x+y; pp=b-x-y; q=c-a-x-y; qp=cp-b-x+y; simplify(p+q+2*x-c), simplify(pp+qp+2*x-cp)
checkable.asserts: q and q' as written satisfy the distance relations (both 0)
p-q'=a+b-c' and p'-q=a+b-c, independent of x,y (both 0)

transcription_corrections: Line 'p + q + 2x = c': in the image the first '+' appears overwritten (looks like a corrected sign). The intended reading is '+', as transcribed.
Struck line before 'f die Brennweite' reads approximately 'Es sei' (deleted), as transcribed.
In 'Hieraus p = nq = (n+1)f' the first '=' is overwritten in the manuscript; the reading is correct.
In 'Entfern. des ersten Hauptebne vom Object' Gauss writes 'des' (sic, for 'der').
The q,q' line reads 'q.q' ... zweiten ... Bilde', with the deleted words 'Br E' and 'zweiten' interlined above.
